source.title: Automatic Perturbation Analysis on General Computational Graphs
source.authors: Kaidi Xu; Zhouxing Shi; Huan Zhang; Minlie Huang; Kai-Wei Chang; B. Kailkhura; X. Lin; Cho-Jui Hsieh

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. Its title differs from the catalog title: the text is titled “Automatic Perturbation Analysis for Scalable Certified Robustness and Beyond.”
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies batch size and reports test accuracy, and compares naturally trained models with models trained using a flatness objective. Its flatness measure and training setup differ from the claim versions’ specified sharpness comparison.
record.gate_note: Most experiments concern certified robustness and do not bear on the claim. The relevant results are the MLP flat-objective experiments in Figure 3 and Table 9. Table 9 measures certified flatness, not training-test gaps or the magnitude-aware sharpness measure specified in V7.
record.test_reason: Figure 3a reports the batch-size/test-accuracy relationship in a new setting: small-data MNIST and FashionMNIST MLPs. This bears on V5, although equal epoch budgets are not established. The certified-flatness experiments do not test V7's specified relationship between magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: flat-objective models generally achieve better test accuracy, especially at very large batch sizes, offering tentative evidence for a flatness/generalization connection. The authors acknowledge possible side effects of the objective and do not claim to prove the hypothesis. The paper's main contribution is automatic LiRPA and scalable certified robustness.
record.recipe_differences: The batch-size experiments use a three-layer MLP, small subsets of MNIST and FashionMNIST, and compare regular cross entropy with a LiRPA-certified flat objective. The optimizer is SGD; no comparison matching the original batch-size studies’ settings is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy is reported across dataset, training-data fraction, batch size, and objective. The authors say accuracy generally decreases with increased batch size, while flat-objective accuracy tends to be better, especially at very large batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: Flat-objective training lowers certified local cross-entropy variation in every matched Table 9 comparison. Evaluation perturbation radii are scaled by each layer's weight norm. Figure 3a's discussion reports generally better test accuracy, especially at very large batches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizing a LiRPA upper bound on perturbed training loss reduces certified local loss variation and can improve held-out accuracy in small-data MLPs; this does not establish V7's sharpness/generalization-gap ranking.

record.peer_reviewed: 34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2020)
record.problems: The flatness and test-accuracy comparison uses small-data MLP experiments and the authors acknowledge that improvements may come from side effects of the flat objective. Figure 3 test-accuracy values are plotted without reported numerical values or uncertainty. The text does not state whether the batch-size comparison holds epoch count fixed.
record.rows_left_out: None. Figure 3a does not provide recoverable exact values for the individual test-accuracy conditions; these are retained as figure-only rows rather than estimated from the plot.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and matched natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning; using different optimizers in unrelated experiments is not a comparison.

The fixed-epoch-budget condition is unconfirmed. Workload-dependent thresholds, longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, and normalization changes are not isolated. The text does not establish that the flat objective removes the within-objective batch-size penalty.

Generalization-gap rankings among similarly low-training-loss convolutional networks and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures. Layer-norm-scaled certified cross-entropy variation in MLPs is a related measure, not the specified test.
Memorization-based removal versus matched random removal and subsequent test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The missing epoch-budget specification is an evidential limitation, not a demonstrated scope failure. Better large-batch accuracy under another objective alone does not justify limits_scope for V5. Individual Figure 3a states remain indeterminate because the supplied text preserves no readable curve values; the aggregate verdict rests on the authors' explicit textual trend. Table 9 values are accurate, but observed was inappropriate as a claim-effect state for rows linked to no version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and generalization on natural labels.
Network width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance.

Whether a batch-size penalty depends on workload or is removed by longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization changes; the text does not state that epoch budgets are fixed.

The specified magnitude-aware perturbation measure, training-test gap comparisons among similarly low-training-loss networks in one convolutional family, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures. The paper instead studies certified loss variation under normalized weight perturbations in MLPs.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Overall batch-size trend in three-layer MLPs on 1% or 10% of MNIST and FashionMNIST; equal epoch budgets unconfirmed
relationships.reason: The Figure 3a discussion explicitly reports generally decreasing test accuracy with increasing batch size (R1–R24); this supports the directional relationship, without establishing the fixed-budget condition or every individual contrast.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports generally decreasing test accuracy with increasing batch size, but the comparisons and equal epoch budgets remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MNIST and FashionMNIST MLP experiments with 1% or 10% of training data and the tested batch sizes
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that test accuracy generally decreases as batch size increases, but also say flat-objective models tend to do better, especially at very large batch size; fixed epoch budgets are not stated. Figure 3a rows R1–R24.
